attempted_claim: The set of Borel codes for 3-regular acyclic Borel graphs admitting a Borel proper 3-edge-coloring is Sigma^1_2-complete, so no Borel or analytic characterization exists, and the hardness reduction preserves determinacy-game witnesses yielding a matching Omega(log n) deterministic LOCAL obstruction family for 3-edge-coloring cubic trees.
claim_type: Borel-versus-measurable chromatic dichotomy with game-transfer lower-bound witness
decisive_failure: No part of the Sigma^1_2-completeness or LOCAL-transfer target was proved; no emergent finding is claimed because the counting lemma is elementary folklore. Evidence is limited to the blocked-route analysis and the replayable gadget-boundary script.

problem_statement: Fix standard Borel codes for 3-regular acyclic Borel graphs on Polish space. Let E3 be the set of codes whose graph admits a Borel proper edge-coloring with 3 colors. Determine the descriptive complexity of E3, specifically whether E3 is Sigma^1_2-complete, and whether the hardness reduction can be chosen to preserve the Marks-game to LOCAL transfer so that hard instances carry Omega(log n) LOCAL edge-coloring obstructions.
record_title: Descriptive Complexity of Borel 3-Edge-Colorability for 3-Regular Acyclic Graphs
